body: Look at supply, not demand. (1) Find industries where capacity growth has stalled - years of poor returns, no new projects, weak players exiting or being acquired. (2) Own the survivors with the best cost position and balance sheet ('last man standing'); as demand catches up with frozen supply, utilisation and pricing rise and margins expand sharply. (3) Prefer high asset-turnover, capital-light models where incremental growth needs little capex. (4) Exit when the industry starts announcing big capacity additions or new entrants rush in. Indicators for Indian investors: capacity utilisation data (cement, steel, paper), industry capex announcements, consolidation deals, number of listed players and their losses, P/B near cycle lows. Related evidence: the Indian capital goods index took ~2007-2021 to regain its peak after a capacity boom - the inverse of this strategy. Risk: demand may never return (structural decline).
title: Andrade: supply-side capital cycle, last man standing
